findings.title: MetricAlertDetectorHandler is abstract and cannot be instantiated
findings.body: Changing `MetricAlertDetectorHandler` to subclass `StatefulDetectorHandler` with only `pass` leaves it abstract because it does not implement `counter_names`, `get_dedupe_value`, `get_group_key_values`, or the new `build_occurrence_and_event_data`. Python will raise `TypeError: Can't instantiate abstract class MetricAlertDetectorHandler...` when `Detector.detector_handler` tries to instantiate `MetricAlertFire.detector_handler`, so processing any detector of this type now crashes instead of yielding no results. Implement the required abstract methods or keep this handler on `DetectorHandler` until it is ready. The TODO comment above is also stale now.

findings.title: Expected occurrence in TestEvaluateGroupKeyValue.test_dedupe uses the wrong group key
findings.body: The expected occurrence is built for group key `val1`, but the call under test uses `group_key` (`expected_result.group_key`). `build_occurrence_and_event_data` derives the fingerprint from the group key, so the actual occurrence has fingerprint `[id:group_key]` while the expected occurrence has `[id:val1]`. The equality assertion in this test will fail; build the expected occurrence with `group_key` instead.

findings.title: StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate docstring still documents a list return
findings.body: The method now returns `dict[DetectorGroupKey, DetectorEvaluationResult]`, but its docstring still says it returns a list of `DetectorEvaluationResult`. This is misleading for callers and subclass implementers.

findings.title: Mock occurrence helper ignores the value argument
findings.body: `build_mock_occurrence_and_event` accepts `value` but never uses it, so the tests do not verify that `evaluate_group_key_value` passes the per-group value into the new occurrence hook. For example, `test_state_results_multi_group` builds group_2's expected occurrence with value 6 even though the packet contains 10, and the test still passes. A regression that passed the wrong value to `build_occurrence_and_event_data` would not be caught; use the value in the expected occurrence or assert the call explicitly.
